fields.v: Rehan, T. (2026). Test-Driven AI Agent Definition (TDAD): Compiling Tool-Using Agents from Behavioral Specifications. arXiv:2603.08806v1 [cs.SE], 9 Mar 2026
Preprint — arXiv v1 (9 Mar 2026); no venue stated
Industry: Fiverr Labs (single author)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — TDAD methodology with reference implementation, evaluated on 4 specs x 2 versions x 3 trials; SpecSuite-Core benchmark (4 specs + generators + harness) as an explicit contribution. No comparison with other approaches
TDAD (Test-Driven AI Agent Definition); version Not stated (reference implementation in github.com/f-labs-io/tdad-paper-code)

YAML specification (tools with schemas/failure modes/sequencing, prioritised policies, decision tree, response contract via a 'respond' tool, optional test_guidance, mutation intents); executable pytest tests split visible (40-70%) / hidden (30-60%), typed MFT/INV/DIR; deterministic fixtures with canary values; compiled artefact = system prompt + tool-description overrides; mutation-intent catalog; v1->v2 spec for evolution with held-out v1 invariant tests

Human writes spec (PRD + decision tree) -> TestSmith (coding agent) generates visible + hidden tests and fixtures from the spec -> PromptSmith (coding agent) iterates the prompt until visible tests pass (Algorithm 1: outer loop, focused inner loop when <10 failures) -> hidden tests measure generalisation (HPR) -> MutationSmith (evaluation only) generates faulty prompt variants, harness checks visible tests kill them (MS) -> spec evolution: v2 compiled from the v1 artefact against v2 tests, v1 invariant tests held out (SURS)

Not stated as review gates. Human (product team / engineer) writes the spec and test guidance; pipeline otherwise automated. Production mode: failing hidden tests promoted to visible and agent recompiled. Human clarification of conflicting tests suggested only as future extension
Full workflow (all roles run end to end on 4 specs, v1 and v2)

Not stated in Böckeler terms. Authors: 'The specification is the single source of truth. Tests implement the specification; they don't define it'; prompt treated as a 'compiled artifact' regenerated from the spec. Closest to spec-as-source (draft, to check)
fields.why: No SDD terms used. 'The specification is the single source of truth' and the prompt as 'compiled artifact' (p. 2-3) suggest spec-as-source, but v2 compilation 'starts from the v1 prompt artifact' (p. 5), closer to spec-anchored; and the generated artefact is an agent prompt, not application code.

fields.v: New artefact compiled from a spec (an LLM agent's prompt and tool descriptions, not application code); v2 evolves the v1 artefact. No existing code base
4 specs, 10-14 decision nodes each; V1 visible tests 34-47 per spec (median over 3 trials, ±10-30%); 5-7 mutation intents per spec. Other Table 3 columns jumbled in text extraction (check PDF)
fields.why: Table 3 (p. 6) is jumbled. Nodes (12, 10, 14, 11) and V1 visible (47, 34, 39, 47) map cleanly. A tentative row-wise reading of the remaining 16 numbers is (V1 hid, V2 vis, V2 hid, Mut): SupportOps 45/53/43/7, DataInsights 42/53/43/6, IncidentRunbook 42/42/45/7, ExpenseGuard 45/46/42/7; it fits the failed-run counts 52/53 and 44/46 (p. 7) and IncidentRunbook's 7 mutations (p. 6), but must be checked in the PDF before use.

Compilation success (all visible tests pass within budget); VPR (visible pass rate); HPR (hidden pass rate); SURS (share of held-out v1 invariant tests passing after v2 compilation)

Automatic: pytest harness asserting on tool-call traces with deterministic fixtures and PII canary detection; no LLM judge or user simulator; mutants killed by harness; cost from API pricing

TDAD + Claude Code (version n.s.) + Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) for all roles; Built Agent run with Claude Agent SDK. Criterion: compilation success (visible tests all pass within 6 outer / 8 inner iterations), HPR, MS, SURS. Values (Table 4-5, successful runs): v1 compile 11/12 (92%), HPR 97.3±2.6%, MS 95.9±7.1%, cost $2.32±0.96, 3.1±0.8 iterations; v2 compile 7/12 (58%), HPR 77.7±13.9% (lowest 51.1%), MS 100%, SURS 97.2±3.5%, cost $2.81±1.71, 2.9±1.1 iterations; total $45.15 for 18 successful runs. Quality: works (v1), partly (v2). Cost: works ($2-3 per spec version)

No comparison of configurations. Single configuration on 4 specs x 2 versions x 3 trials = 24 runs. Baseline: none (seed prompts said to reach 0-90% VPR before compilation, not tabulated; DSPy, TextGrad, APE not compared). Held constant: same model and default temperature for all roles, budget 6 outer / 8 inner iterations, Docker isolation. Acceptance tests: hidden tests generated per trial by TestSmith, withheld from PromptSmith. Repetitions: 3 per spec version. Human intervention: none stated
N/A (no comparison). Only qualitative claim that compilation improves on seed prompts in all cases; no numbers, no significance test

N/A as a comparison. The evaluation method (hidden tests, mutation testing, SURS) surfaced test gaps (2 surviving v1 mutants) and showed variance across 3 trials (v1 HPR ±2-4%, v2 ±4-16%). Limitations stated: tests regenerated per trial; excluding non-activating mutants may overstate MS; no ablation of anti-gaming mechanisms; RPR not computed

Requirements must be encodable as behavioural tests ('be empathetic' resists); mutation testing cannot guarantee completeness; gaming risk reduced not eliminated; stochastic variation; 30-60 min and $2-3 per spec version may be prohibitive for rapid prototyping; TestSmith self-censors hostile inputs (human-curated corpora needed); only 4 specs, 3 trials, one model (Claude Sonnet 4.5), no ablation, no comparison to DSPy/TextGrad/APE; scaling to 50+ nodes and authoring learning curve not quantified. Future: PromptSmith escalating to TestSmith for conflicting tests

Tables 3 and 4 columns jumbled in pdftotext; values used are from the text (§6, abstract) where they match Table 4 aggregates (92%/58%, 97.3%/77.7%, SURS 97.2%). Inconsistencies: (1) text says all failed runs with logs reached >95% VPR but lists IncidentRunbook/v1 at 36/38 (94.7%) (p. 7); (2) hidden-test share given as 30-60% in §4.1 (p. 4) but 40-60% in §5.1 (p. 5); (3) convergence 'typically 2-5 iterations' (§3.6, p. 4) vs 'most converge in 2-4' (§6.5, p. 7). Abstract '97% mean hidden pass rate' = Table 4 97.3%. V2 failures: 2 conflicting tests, 3 budget exhausted. Table 6 shows only 4 of 5-7 mutation intents per spec. Built object is an LLM agent prompt, not program code. Replication package: GitHub repo with all 4 specs, harness, Docker; generated tests/fixtures/results only for SupportOps. Pre-registration: not claimed. Language: Python (pytest), YAML specs

fields.why: v2 weakness and surviving mutants are reported, but 'compilation consistently adds value' (p. 7) rests on seed-prompt VPRs not tabulated, anti-gaming mechanisms are not ablated, and 'all failed runs ... achieved >95% VPR' is contradicted by the 94.7% case on the same page. Partly is reasonable; Yes is arguable.
